---
title: "Two meanings of one glyph"
---

This small website demonstrates scoped notation preferences with original synthetic content. The declarations and alternative notation are author-approved examples; mathematical equivalence and the operation laws require independent review.

## Distinct concepts

The first concept is [synthetic composition]{#term-composition} in the algebra scope. Its annotated expression is [$x \circ y$]{.maths-notation profile="composition" arg-left="x" arg-right="y"}.

The second concept is [synthetic probability combination]{#term-probability-combination} in the probability scope. Its annotated expression is [$x \circ y$]{.maths-notation profile="probability-combination" arg-left="x" arg-right="y"}. This demonstration declares a distinct operation name and scope; it supplies no probability law or numerical calculation.

An ordinary, unannotated expression such as $x \circ y$ keeps its authored notation. The generated definition below likewise keeps its authored operation: its mathematical parameters are separate from these annotated preference occurrences.

## Defining associativity

The [associativity condition]{#concept-associativity} has its own concept identity. The following native definition has a separate assertion identity and a declared `defines` relation to that concept. The template states the condition that a closed binary operation would need to satisfy.

::: {#def-associativity .maths-instance template="associativity" carrier="G" operation="\circ" name="Associativity condition"}
:::

See @def-associativity for the condition and the glossary below for its explicit dependencies.

## Choose notation

Select an approved notation for each concept. The same glyph can have different choices in the two scopes. The controls offer authored-default reset and optional local persistence; the [second page](second.qmd) contains the same annotated concepts and its own controls.
